clue.text: Negotiate track up mountain, perhaps

indicators.note: to negotiate a route is to work your way round it, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A climber plans a route up a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Negotiate' is the anagram signal; read whole, the clue points at its own comma, printed just before 'perhaps', as an example of the thing defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A comma, like the one printed in the clue itself, is one example of a written sign used to separate words in a sentence.

clue.text: More determined to take rest during drive

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the span of the other

parts.note: to drive a car is to steer it
to rest is to lie down

explanation.surface: A motorist gets more resolute about taking a break on a long drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Steelier means harder and more resolute, a synonym for more determined.

clue.text: Small stuff, get lost!

parts.note: to stuff is to cram

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a petty matter and tells the speaker to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are rude commands telling someone to leave at once, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Take this clue number, change it and lose your mind!

indicators.note: change it tells the solver to rearrange the letters just gathered

parts.note: this is clue 4, so the number is four

explanation.surface: An instruction so baffling that it drives the solver mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this clue number' is the clue's own number, 4, written as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: To freak out is an informal idiom for panicking or losing control of oneself.

clue.text: One driven to have hip operations given worrying discharge

parts.note: a car is something that is driven
the hip is a bone
military operations are missions

explanation.surface: A motorist due for hip surgery is upset by some leaking fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhaust gases released into the air are a pollutant discharge that causes concern about climate.

clue.text: See 5
Fish — perch, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a perch is a place to sit

explanation.surface: Two kinds of fish are compared, perch being given as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' looks like the fish, but here it is a resting spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaice is a flatfish commonly eaten in Britain, so it is an example of fish.

clue.text: Description of microcephalic organism that doesn't impress me?

definitions.text: Description of microcephalic organism that doesn't impress me?

parts.words: Description of microcephalic organism that doesn't impress me?
parts.note: a creature with an abnormally small head is literally small and of small brain; the same words are a stock put-down of showing off

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up a tiny-headed creature and is unimpressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Microcephalic means having a small head, so such a creature is neither large nor bright; the phrase is also a well-known British catchphrase used to deflate boasting.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase is said to dismiss behaviour as unimpressive, while literally describing a small, dim creature.

clue.text: Rash was 'armful — I see "Your Tiny Hand Is Frozen"?

parts.note: something harmful hurt, and with the dropped H of the Cockney apostrophe it becomes 'urt
C sounds like the word see
the English title of a famous aria from Puccini's opera La Boheme

explanation.surface: A tenor with a blotchy arm laments while singing a Puccini number.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'armful shows a dropped H, so the matching hurt also loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Urticaria is the medical name for hives, a skin condition seen as an itchy red rash.

clue.text: Fine act clumsily backfiring in part

indicators.note: backfiring says the hidden letters are read backwards
in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is penalised for a clumsy act that partly backfired.
explanation.definitionFit: To mulct is a formal verb meaning to fine or extract money from someone as a penalty.

clue.text: Search out a girl, seeking fate

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: Sara is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man hunts for a girlfriend, hoping destiny will help.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase means whatever will be, will be, an expression of accepting fate.

clue.text: Head back holding sparkler as defence

indicators.note: holding says one piece contains the other
back says the word is read in reverse

parts.note: nob is slang for the head
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: Someone tips their head back to drink fizz as a protective measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A bastion is a fortified projecting part of a wall, a structure built for defence.

clue.text: Only one item, you fool

parts.note: U is text-speak for you
a nit is a fool

explanation.surface: A shopper with a single purchase is called an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing counted on its own, one individual item.

clue.text: Correspondent finds cash and passport among foreign money

parts.note: coin is cash

indicators.note: among says one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a cent is a coin used in the USA and the eurozone
a passport is a form of identification, ID

explanation.surface: A journalist abroad turns up money and travel documents in a currency stash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspondent' looks like the reporter, but it is the adjective meaning matching.
explanation.definitionFit: As adjectives, both mean corresponding or happening together in agreement.

clue.text: See 8
Those who came go away

parts.note: a go in a game is a turn
away from home is out

explanation.surface: The guests who attended are told to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnout is the number of people who attend an event, the attendance.

clue.text: Boy meets girl with one tongue

parts.note: Ben is a boy's name
gal is an informal word for a girl
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A romance starts as a boy meets a girl and they share a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengali is the language of Bangladesh and West Bengal, and a tongue is a language.

clue.text: So cut evidence?

definitions.meaning: used as an intensifier in British slang it means very
flowing blood is a sign that someone has been cut

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a wound proves the point.
explanation.walkthrough: The British slang intensifier, a mild swear word, works like 'so' or 'very'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a British intensifier like very and the visible sign of a wound.

clue.text: Those who are offside, perhaps?

parts.note: read as off side, the players are the side that is not at home

explanation.surface: A question about footballers caught beyond the last defender.
explanation.walkthrough: Offside is a football infringement, but split as off side it means the visiting team, away from its home ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The visiting side plays off its own ground, so it is literally the side that is off.

clue.text: Done too much, having done reasonably to open old school

parts.note: when something is done it is over

indicators.note: to open says one piece is set inside the other, splitting it

parts.note: co-ed is a dated name for a mixed school
done reasonably is done OK

explanation.surface: A pupil overachieves after doing fairly well when starting at a former school.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is overcooked has been cooked for too long, done more than enough.

clue.text: Slip and run it

parts.note: to slip is to err, make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone trips up and has to dash off.
explanation.walkthrough: One runs an errand, so 'run it' describes the answer as the thing run.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short trip made on someone's behalf, something one is said to run.

clue.text: Choose chapter during one's light study

parts.note: to choose is to opt

indicators.note: during says one piece is set within the other

parts.note: one's read as one is gives I + S

explanation.surface: A student picks a chapter while doing some easy reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light study' looks like easy reading, but it is the science of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Optics is the branch of physics dealing with the behaviour of light.

clue.text: See 11
Still water rising for boat

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: pools are bodies of still water

explanation.surface: A pond's level climbs high enough for a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a one-masted sailing vessel, a type of boat.

clue.text: Musical device right to move in modern time

indicators.note: to move tells the solver to shift a letter to another spot

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer modernises a piece by shifting its rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: A mordent is a musical ornament, a rapid alternation with an adjacent note.

clue.text: Managed to grip instrument, though weak

indicators.note: to grip says one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: to have managed is to have done, did
a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A frail player still manages to hold the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Something diluted is watered down and therefore weak.

clue.text: Field grazing area

definitions.meaning: a field of operation or expertise, its scope
open land where cattle roam, as in the American West

explanation.surface: A farmer looks over a pasture.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a scope or field and open grazing land for livestock.

clue.text: Certainly not a kid, boy soldier

parts.note: to kid is to con
a boy is a son
a soldier ant is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: A young soldier insists he is no child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Certainly not a' looks like a denial, but means a letter that is certainly not the vowel A.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter that is not a vowel can never be the letter A, which is a vowel.
